selected.rationale: The Affluent Classic shares a direct affinity for home goods and values quality and craftsmanship over trends, perfectly aligning with the advertiser's Portugal-made linen and grown-up aesthetic.
The Sustainability Buyer looks for supply chain transparency and authentic craftsmanship, which matches the advertiser's emphasis on breathability and made-in-Portugal origin.
The Wellness Optimizer treats sleep as a core system and is willing to pay premium prices, making breathable, high-end linen a strong product fit for their sleep-optimization goals.

rejected.reason: The Busy Parent seeks convenience, bulk buying, and subscriptions, whereas the advertiser offers a one-off, premium-positioned luxury bedding product.
The Gen Z Aesthete prefers playful novelty and a typical AOV of $48, which is far too low for a premium $200 AOV bedding brand targeting ages 30-55.
The Pet Parent focuses entirely on pet health, supplies, and food, which has no category overlap with human bedding and linen.
The Convenience-First Millennial prioritizes instant delivery and one-click subscriptions, clashing with the advertiser's one-off, artisanal home goods business model.
The Value-Conscious Shopper is high in price sensitivity and responds to discounts and bundles, whereas the advertiser is positioned as a premium, non-Brooklinen alternative.
The Fitness Enthusiast focuses on activewear, supplements, and recovery, which does not connect to the home bedding and linen category.
The Gifter is a temporary seasonal mode rather than a core long-term customer base, and they are disinterested in self-care-only framing compared to permanent home upgrades.
